messages.text: On it! Will review this afternoon. Quick question: are we storing the PKCE code verifier server-side or client-side?

elements.text: On it! Will review this afternoon. Quick question: are we storing the PKCE code verifier server-side or client-side?

messages.text: Client-side in sessionStorage — it's generated fresh per auth attempt and deleted after exchange. Server never sees the verifier, only the code challenge (which is public anyway).

messages.text:
Smart. sessionStorage is scoped to the tab/window so it can't leak across tabs. Good call. 

One concern: the token refresh mutex — if the first refresh fails, do queued requests get unblocked with an error or do they retry?

elements.text: Smart. sessionStorage is scoped to the tab/window so it can’t leak across tabs. Good call.
One concern: the token refresh mutex — if the first refresh fails, do queued requests get unblocked with an error or do they retry?

messages.text: They get rejected with the error and the caller decides whether to retry (usually means redirect to login). We don't retry internally to avoid cascading failures.

elements.text: They get rejected with the error and the caller decides whether to retry (usually means redirect to login). We don’t retry internally to avoid cascading failures.
